success_patterns: Clue text found verbatim in an archive page (J! Archive, StudyStack flashcards, TriviaBistro), with the answer after the clue or recoverable from other passages. Chicago and Max Factor were answered this way. Rule 3 already covers it.

Archive snippet truncated after the clue (Max Factor, Gadsden Purchase): the agent took the entity that recurs across many passage titles and details. Already covered by the truncated-archive-snippet rule.

Person clues ('author of Gai-Jin', 'singer who recorded Welcome to My Nightmare', 'Uncle Walter') were answered with the bare, commonly used full name (James Clavell, Alice Cooper, Walter Cronkite). Already covered by the person-name and nickname rules.

Head-noun exception applied correctly: 'Gadsden Purchase' kept its head word because the bare modifier would be incomplete. 'Divine Comedy' was a title answered without extra descriptors. Both are covered by Rule 4.

Trade-name and brand clue (methylphenidate -> Ritalin): the single name that recurs across nearly all passages was chosen over the less frequent alternatives (Concerta, Metadate). Covered by 'choose the entity the passages repeatedly tie to the clue'.

patch.reasoning: Every success in this batch follows behaviour the skill already encodes: scan for verbatim archive hits, complete truncated snippets from recurring entities, use short standard name forms, and keep head nouns only when the bare word would be incomplete. Earlier steps in this epoch show that adding more rules lowered the score. I am proposing no edits so the working rules stay intact.
